hyps.why: Replacing a missing direct input-to-output edge with a 3x3 conv adds a whole path, which helps more than upgrading an existing operation.
Adding a skip path where the edge was absent gives a larger gain than swapping one existing op for a skip.
A strong direct 0->3 conv already supplies capacity, so the extra gain from a conv on edge 5 is smaller.
Replacing a missing edge into the output with a conv adds a path, a larger gain than upgrading an existing op.
With edge 1 absent, edge 0 is the only way into node 1, so removing it cuts connectivity and hurts more.
With edge 5 absent, the paths through node 2 into the output are weaker, so removing edge 0 loses more.
Without the direct 0->3 edge, removing edge 0 removes much of the network's remaining input pathway.
When the direct 0->3 edge is absent, the benefit of a heavier conv on edge 0 is smaller or negative, as in experiment 8.
Upgrading an existing 1x1 conv to 3x3 gives a smaller gain than replacing a skip or pool.
If edge 0 is none, node 1 gets no input, so a conv on edge 1->3 has almost nothing to process.
